headline: Approved updated language for the Energy Project Reserve Fund; two other items were tabled.
summary: Members heard an update on net metering rules that the Public Utility Commission (PUC) is rewriting, and public comment on home energy audits, rental building energy performance, and large-building energy reporting. Staff reported on a new fire department electric vehicle, a fast charger at 510 Shelburne Rd, and a Join Fair where committee vacancies can be advertised. Members also approved updated language for a city fund and tabled two agenda items.
decisions: Approved updated language for the Energy Project Reserve Fund (Resolution 2019-1), with Ethan's proposed changes, by unanimous vote.
Tabled agenda items 9 and 10 when the meeting ran out of time.

decision_evidence.quote: MJ moves to adopt the language with Ethan's proposed Changes ... Jean seconds ... Unanimous approval
Committee members tabled items 9 and 10 because it was 8:30PM.

plain_text:
South Burlington Energy Committee
October 28, 2026
The South Burlington Energy Committee held a regular meeting on Wednesday, October 28th
in Room 301, 180 Market St. and by Zoom remote participation.
Members present: Jean Sebastien Chaulot, Steve Crowley (Chair), Carrie McLaughlin, MJ
Reale (Vice-Chair), Leendert Huisman (online starting at 7:40PM)
Also present: Lou Bresee (Energy Project Manager), Paul Conner (Planning and Zoning
Director), Bettina Miguez (Climate Action Manager - online), Beth Zigmund
Member of the public: Ethan Goldman, Peter Jarka-Sellers, Mark Menin, Michael Miller (sp?),
Talia Rizzo
Welcome and Agenda review 
At 6:35PM no quorum: Committee decided to continue meeting understanding that no policy
decisions could be made, so that members could hear guest presentation.
Item 5 moved up to after public comment.
Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda:
Peter Jarka-Sellers from Run On Climate discussing three policies
Energy Audit requirement when a home is sold with results made clear to buyers.
Energy performance of a rental building.
Large buildings to report energy use and emissions on an annual basis so we have more data
on large buildings 
Steve requests Peter send a memo with details to Steve, Bettina and Beth that we can circulate
to the committee
Talia Rizzo
Support for energy use disclosure for renters - as a renter she feels like this would be really
helpful and this is a good time for it.
[formerly 5] Net Metering Update (REV)
Jonathan Dowds - goal of REV is to protect investments of people who are already net
metering, and make net metering viable moving forward
Net Metering - PUC has opened a rulemaking proceeding
Right now peak demand and solar is not as aligned 
Currently utility is paying too much for off-peak solar
Better align solar with peak demand times
Steer future net metering projects from congested areas
Already taking big hits from federal and state policies
Moving towards incentivizing self-consumption and strategically timed (peak) exports
Full value for behind the meter generation and use
Lower value for exported power
incentivized storage with solar
Goal is to make solar technology accessible and viable for average families
Risk is undervaluing net metering - this may be dependent on administration
Lots of public energy on this topic as reflected by the volume of public comment (over 1000
comments)
PUC is not capturing the full value of net metering
More risk in retroactive changes to the compensation structure
This could blow up the financing 
11/16 PUC Workshop - Vermont Distribution Utilities and future workshops are coming
Looking to finish rulemaking by 2028
Standard Offer projects are locked in
What can the energy committee do?
make people as aware as possible
get as many public comments as possible
public comment is ongoing, but REV is trying to be strategic about when to ask people to do
that
[7:40PM quorum when Leendert joined online]
Updates From Committee Members/Events and conferences attended:
VECAN Energy Committee Roundtable - session to talk about town energy committees
Charlotte, Essex, Milton, Jericho and South Burlington attended
Not much opportunity for collaboration
Milton is moving ahead with balcony solar
Included VGS, GMP and VEIC
Staff Reports
Lou
Fire department is buying another EV
Renewable Diesel proposal has gone in - will hear mid-November on the grant
Paul
Vermont Climate Assessment Group launched their report last Friday (third iteration) on how
climate change is impacting Vermont.
All input came from student projects
Bettina
Sent in charging smart scorecard - likely to get the Silver designation
Met with Eli from GMP - Fast charging at 510 Shelburne Rd should be ready soon, SPAN
(smart panel) pilots, heat pump rate pilot with O'Brien neighborhood
Building and Thermal Implementation Group - Keith and Ethan are delegates
Ethan to continue representing
Join Fair - movie Join or Die in library auditorium - opportunity to advertise vacancies for
committees.
November 15th - Would like to have somebody there to represent the committee - we will have
somebody
Energy Project Reserve Fund - (revolving fund) - Resolution 2019-1: updated language
because what we are doing is a bit broader in scope than the current language allows for.  Lou
says he would like to take it to Council quickly to officially update the language 
MJ moves to adopt the language with Ethan's proposed Changes
Jean seconds
Unanimous approval
Committee members tabled items 9 and 10 because it was 8:30PM.
To-do items:
Action:  Jonathan to share slides with the committee and keep us updated through Bettina (or
Carrie)
Action:  Bettina to ask Peter for memo with details that we can circulate to the committee
Action: Bettina to let Mira know that Energy Committee will participate in Join Fair.
Adjourn. Meeting was adjourned at 8:30PM. Next meeting is November 18, 2026.
